The transition from horses to cars as the dominant mode of transport did not happen in a single year; instead, it unfolded over roughly two decades depending on region and counting method. In major cities like New York, London, and Paris, traffic counts already showed more cars than horses by 1912 [d10]. For central Europe, estimates place the crossover around 1925–1930 [d10]. In the United States, some sources suggest the late 1920s as the period when cars outnumbered horses nationally [d1, d7], while others document rapid adoption by 1917 without asserting exact parity [d4]. A late local benchmark comes from Chicago in 1940, where cars overwhelmingly outnumbered horse-drawn vehicles [d9].
